In [[mathematics]], a '''Novikov–Shubin invariant''', introduced by {{harvs|txt|last1=Novikov|first1=Sergei|author1-link=Sergei Novikov (mathematician)|last2=Shubin|first2=Mikhail|author2-link=Mikhail Shubin (mathematician)| year=1986}}, is an invariant of a compact [[Riemannian manifold]] related to the [[spectrum (functional analysis)|spectrum]] of the [[Laplace operator]] acting on square-integrable [[differential form]]s on its universal cover.

The Novikov–Shubin invariant gives a measure of the density of eigenvalues around zero. It can be computed from a [[Triangulation (topology)|triangulation]] of the manifold, and it is a [[homotopy|homotopy invariant]]. In particular, it does not depend on the chosen Riemannian metric on the manifold.{{sfn|Lück|2002|p=104, Theorem 2.67}}
